title: Message/set: sentAt from owner client stored as-is with no validation or clamping
description: process_create (message.rs:391-394) extracts sentAt as an optional string and passes it directly to insert_outbound_message as sent_at_peer. No RFC 3339 validation, no future-date clamping, no past-date sanity check. The readAt field has a clamp (line 627: min(now_unix + 60)), but sentAt has none. An owner client can supply sentAt: '1970-01-01T00:00:00Z' or sentAt: '2099-01-01T00:00:00Z'. The peer/architecture doc says sentAt from peers is untrusted, but sentAt from the owner client is also unvalidated. This will corrupt sort order in chat UIs. Fix: validate sentAt as RFC 3339 and apply a similar clamp (e.g. reject if > now + 5 minutes or < some reasonable past bound).
